title: Generators of the integral symplectic group Sp(2n, ℤ)
abstract: For every finite index type n, the integral symplectic group Sp(2n, ℤ) is generated by the matrix J = (0 −1; 1 0), the translations (1 S; 0 1) with S symmetric, and the matrices (U 0; 0 Vᵀ) with UV = VU = 1 (the image of GL(n, ℤ)). The proof does not induct on n. It inducts on a set s of indices: every symplectic matrix that fixes the basis vectors e_j, j ∈ s, of the first half of ℤⁿ ⊕ ℤⁿ lies in the generated subgroup. In the step, the column M e_i = (a, c) is moved to e_i by elements that fix the e_j: first Euclid's algorithm in each coordinate k ∉ s makes c = 0, using (1 tE_kk; 0 1) and its conjugate by J; then a descent on the sum of |a_k| over k ∉ s, by units of M_n(ℤ) of the form 1 + c·e_lᵀ, reduces a to e_i, the last nonzero entry being ±1 because a row of the inverse matrix gives a Bezout relation.
